comparison: Both evaluate the HiCapR method and its technical specifications (C1, C2, C33-C46, C132-C139). OpenEval finds the method well-validated with robust performance metrics and rates it SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers acknowledge potential strengths but express UNCERTAIN evaluation due to concerns about reproducibility (single vs. multiple biological replicates) and insufficient method description.

Perfect claim overlap (C3-C5, C51-C56, C63-C64, C141-C142) regarding detection of known HIV-1 structural elements. Both agree these confirmatory findings are well-supported. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as technical validation, peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, noting no specific challenges to these canonical structure identifications.

Both address novel genome-wide homodimerization peaks (C6-C8, C71-C73, C154). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting detection is supported but functional roles in splicing/encapsidation are speculative. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, emphasizing extensive computational analysis needs experimental validation, particularly for functional claims.

OpenEval R4 addresses SRSF motifs and mechanistic insights (C74-C81, C155-C157), rating SUPPORTED with caveat that functional implications need testing. Peer R3 covers overlapping claims about dimerization sites and functional roles, rating UNCERTAIN due to insufficient experimental validation of computational predictions.

High claim overlap (C82-C89, C158-C160) on spatial relationship between dimers and splicing sites. Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes strong observational data but speculative functional roles without experimental validation. Peer reviewers similarly emphasize computational analysis requires experimental support for functional interpretations.

Both evaluate dimers at Gag binding sites and RRE (C90-C94, C161-C162). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED due to experimental validation via multiple orthogonal methods. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting validation is 'marginally better' but criticizing precision of Kd determinations and emphasizing need for more experimental validation.

Both address RRE local structure and functional implications (C95-C97). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting structural observation is supported but functional roles are speculative. Peer R8 also rates UNCERTAIN, emphasizing functional interpretations about RRE conformation and rev-RRE interaction lack experimental support.

Both evaluate genomic domain identification and persistence (C102-C112, C166-C167). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on robust quantitative data and statistical backing. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, accepting computational identification appears robust but emphasizing functional interpretations as structural scaffolds lack experimental validation.

Both address differential long-range interactions between cells and virions (C9-C11, C113-C117, C130-C131, C143-C144, C150-C151). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on multiple analytical approaches and quantitative data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging valuable data but noting incomplete analysis based on limited datasets requiring experimental validation.

Both evaluate persistent domains and their enrichment at dimer interfaces (C12-C14, C37). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting observations are well-documented but functional role as structural scaffolds is speculative. Peer R5 similarly rates UNCERTAIN, emphasizing computational identification is robust but functional interpretations lack experimental support.

Both address viewpoint analysis of 5'-UTR interactions (C118-C129, C143-C144, C146, C148). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on figure-supported data and comparative observations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting functional interpretations about RNA transport and nuclear export are speculative without direct experimental validation.

Partial overlap on technical performance metrics (C38-C46, C49). OpenEval R1 includes these in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of HiCapR method. Peer R6 focuses specifically on reproducibility concerns, rating UNCERTAIN due to discrepancies in biological replicate reporting and timing of replicate generation.

OpenEval R12 addresses sequence variation between HIV-1 strains and structural conservation (C57-C62, C70), rating SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these strain comparison claims.

OpenEval R13 validates 5'-UTR dimerization against established structural data (C65-C69), rating SUPPORTED as technical validation. While peer R3 includes C65, C68-C69 in broader evaluation, no peer result specifically focuses on this validation aspect.

OpenEval R14 addresses alternative mechanistic hypotheses about dimer-domain relationships (C168-C171), rating UNCERTAIN as speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these mechanistic hypotheses.

OpenEval R15 evaluates speculation about rod-like structure in virions (C152-C153), rating UNCERTAIN as hypothesis lacking direct structural data. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses this specific structural model speculation.

OpenEval R16 addresses broad interpretations about genome folding importance and functional roles (C36, C148, C165), rating UNCERTAIN as reasonable but requiring validation. Peer R9 includes C148 but focuses on different claim subset; no peer result specifically evaluates these broad interpretive claims.
